changes.text: 还需要四个人。队长决定征求志愿者，同时老老实实写明：他心里其实基本知道会选谁——「I pretty well knew which of the people I would select」。他召集众人，说明计划，征求志愿者，许多人当即站了出来。克林（Crean）原本被安排留在岛上当怀尔德的帮手，他恳求随行，与怀尔德商量之后，队长答应带上他。挑人的标准也摆在明处：有人不够强壮，担不动船上的活；有人不是熟练水手，在船上派不上用场。

Four more were needed. He decided to call for volunteers while admitting, honestly, that he already had a pretty good idea of his choices — "I pretty well knew which of the people I would select". He called the men together, explained his plan and asked for volunteers; many came forward at once. Crean had been slated to stay behind as Wild's right-hand man, but he begged so hard for a place in the boat that, after consulting Wild, the leader promised to take him. The criteria were stated openly: some were not fit for the work the boat would demand, and others, not seasoned sailors, would be of little use aboard.
两位医生麦基尔罗伊（McIlroy）和麦克林（Macklin）都想随行，但明白自己的职责是留在岛上照顾病号。有人提议把双脚冻伤的布莱克博罗（Blackborrow）带上船，让他尽快得到温暖和庇护。队长否掉了这个提议。记录里给的理由是存活推断：健康的人在船上都难活；他看不出一个躺在舱底、动弹不得的病人，怎么可能熬过必定会遇到的坏天气。

The two doctors, McIlroy and Macklin, were both anxious to go but realized that their duty lay on the island with the sick men. One proposal was to take Blackborrow, the man with the frostbitten feet, so that he could have shelter and warmth as quickly as possible. The leader vetoed it. The record gives survival reasoning: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and he did not see how a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could possibly survive the heavy weather they were sure to encounter.
小船的加固是拼凑而成的，很简陋，但足以给一层帆布覆罩打底。帆布冻得硬邦邦，只能先裁好，再在脂肪炉上一英尺一英尺地烤开，才能缝成覆罩，最后钉好、拧紧。覆罩装上后确实给了小船一层安全的样子，可队长心里不踏实，觉得它「bore a strong likeness to stage scenery」——看着像花岗石墙，其实不过是帆布和板条。事后证明，这层覆罩确实顶用。

The work on the boat was a patched-up affair, but it provided a base for a canvas covering. The canvas came frozen stiff; it had to be cut and then thawed over the blubber stove foot by foot before it could be sewn into a cover, then nailed and screwed into position. The cover did lend the boat an appearance of safety, but the leader felt uneasy that "it bore a strong likeness to stage scenery" — a wall that looks like granite and is in fact no better than canvas and lath. As events proved, the covering served its purpose well.

航程中有一次，遇上了队长二十六年海上经历中从未见过的巨浪，与多日来那些白浪翻卷的大浪完全不同。他高喊大家抓紧。船被像软木塞一样抛起、向前甩出，灌进半船水，在重击下颤抖；所有人拼命用随手抓到的容器掏水，十分钟后才觉得船重新有了生命。文森特在过去一周已不再是积极的船员，队长写明难以解释他的垮掉——他是船上体格最强壮的人之一，年轻，在北海拖网船上干过，本该比麦卡锡更能吃苦，而麦卡锡没那么强壮，却总是乐呵呵的。淡水减到每人每天半品脱。带上船的冰块早已用完，装船时一只水桶在浪里被撞裂，渗进了一些海水，喝的水发咸，渴得更厉害；队长不肯增加配给，有人恳求预支第二天的水，也被拒绝：万一风向不利，船可能被吹离海岛，航程拖长许多天。原文感叹，缺水是人所能承受的最严酷的匮乏。5月8日中午12点30分，麦卡锡从云隙中望见南乔治亚的黑色悬崖，距离开象岛整十四天。5月10日，他们驶向一处队长认为必定是哈康国王湾（King Haakon Bay）的大海湾；风向转为从湾内吹出，他们在强风中抢风五次，才穿过礁石进入宽阔的湾口。暮色将近，他们转向海湾南岸一处有礁石护着的小湾。小船乘着涌浪触到海滩，几分钟后众人都平安上了岸；他们在脚边发现一条淡水溪流，随即跪下大口痛饮。

At one point came a wave beyond anything the leader had met in twenty-six years at sea — a mighty upheaval of the ocean, quite apart from the white-capped seas that had been their tireless enemies for many days. He shouted for everyone to hold on: "It's got us!" The boat was lifted and flung forward like a cork, half-full of water and shuddering under the blow; the men baled with the energy of men fighting for life, and after ten minutes of uncertainty felt her renew her life beneath them. Vincent had for the past week ceased to be an active member of the crew, and the leader could not easily account for his collapse: physically one of the strongest men in the boat, young, with service on North Sea trawlers, he should have borne hardship better than McCarthy, who was not so strong but always happy. The daily water allowance was cut to half a pint a man. The lumps of ice taken aboard were long gone, and the breaker had been slightly stove in during loading, letting in some sea-water, so the brackish water sharpened the thirst; the leader would not raise the allowance or let anyone draw against the morrow's, however he was begged — should the wind turn unfavourable, it might drive them away from the island and lengthen the voyage by many days. Lack of water, the account adds, is the severest privation men can be condemned to endure. At 12.30 p.m. on May 8, McCarthy caught a glimpse of the black cliffs of South Georgia through a rift in the clouds, just fourteen days after leaving Elephant Island. On May 10 they made for a big indentation the leader thought must be King Haakon Bay; with the wind blowing out of the bay, they tacked five times in the strong wind before getting through the reef into the wide mouth of the bay. With dusk approaching, they turned toward a small cove guarded by a reef on the south side of the bay. The boat ran in on a swell and touched the beach, and in a few minutes they were all safe ashore; finding a stream of fresh water almost at their feet, they were soon down on their knees drinking.
把这几个决定放在一起看，一种解释是：真正让这个方案说得出口的，是最坏情形那笔账。出海的人带一个月口粮，一个月到不了南乔治亚就必死无疑，而留下的人在冬天少了几张要吃饭的嘴；最坏情形被算成：也不会给留下的人增加风险。本文推断，当所有选项都糟透时，人们愿意跟从的未必是更有希望的那条路，而可能是把代价算清楚、不把损失转嫁给同伴的那条路。

Read together, these decisions suggest one explanation: what made the plan speakable was the arithmetic of the worst case. The boat party carried a month's provisions; if they did not make South Georgia within the month, they were sure to go under. The men left behind would have fewer mouths to feed through the winter. The worst case was calculated as adding nothing to the risks of the men left on the island. This piece infers that when every option is grim, people will follow not necessarily the more hopeful road, but the one that costs its losses honestly and does not shift them onto comrades.
拒绝病号上船那一条，读起来最不舒服，但记录里给的是存活推断，不是道德立场：健康的人在船上都难活，在他看来，重病躺舱底的人熬不过坏天气。本文推断，这种取舍的难处不在决定本身，而在它必须给出理由——有人提了建议，被否掉了，记述里写明了否决的理由。原文没有说这些理由是否当众向全队讲过；若是讲过，代价至少由全队一起看见，而不是由某个被悄悄放下的人独自承担，但这只是未经证实的推测。

The refusal of the sick man is the least comfortable paragraph to read, yet the record offers survival reasoning rather than a moral stance: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and in his view a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could not survive the heavy weather. This piece infers that the difficulty of such a trade-off lies less in the decision itself than in having to give reasons for it: a proposal was made and vetoed, and the account sets down why. The original does not say whether those reasons were put to the whole party; if they were, the cost would at least have been visible to everyone rather than borne by one person quietly set aside — but that is an unverified conjecture.
还有一处值得留意：记述说他决定征求志愿者，同时心里基本知道会选谁。原文写明，他召集众人、说明计划、征求志愿者，许多人当即站了出来；但最终的人选仍由他选定。本文提出的一种替代做法是直接点名，省掉征求的形式。一种解释是：先向全队说明计划、详细讲清危险和理由，再征求志愿，可能让名单读起来更像共识而不是指派。这只是一种解释，原文没有说明他为什么这样安排。

One more detail catches the eye: the account says he decided to call for volunteers while already having a pretty good idea of his choices. The original states that he called the men together, explained his plan and asked for volunteers, and that many came forward at once; yet the final selection was still his. One alternative this piece raises would have been simply to name names and skip the formality. One reading is that explaining the plan and arguing the dangers and reasons to the party in detail before asking for volunteers may make the list read as consensus rather than assignment. This is only one reading, and the original gives no reason for the arrangement.
这套记录只有当事人一个史源，是他事后写下的第一人称自述。作者说，南乔治亚航程的记述依据逐日写下的简略笔记，笔记通常只记距离、船位和天气，航程中的具体经过则来自记忆。文中的对话都带有记述性质：把队伍托付给怀尔德的那句交代、克林恳求随行，都未必是逐字原话。队长自述看队员时信心在增加，那是回忆中的自我描述，不是当时可核实的心理记录。

This record rests on exactly one historical source: a first-person account written after the fact by one of those involved. The author says the account of the voyage to South Georgia is based on scanty notes made day by day, which usually dealt with the bare facts of distances, positions and weather, while the incidents themselves came from memory. Its dialogue is reported, not transcribed — the words entrusting the party to Wild, Crean's plea for a place in the boat — and need not be verbatim. The leader's statement that his confidence grew as he looked at the men is retrospective self-description, not a verifiable record of his state of mind at the time.
全文只有当事人一个史源（其事后的第一人称自述）；航程部分据其逐日简略笔记（多为距离、船位、天气）与回忆写成；对话与心理均为记述性内容，未必逐字、不可核实；天数只用原文明确写出的出海第六天和离开象岛第十四天，日期照原文写5月8日、5月10日，所引片段未给公元年份，不做换算；距离、口粮、水的数字照原文写法；原文为扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文。

The whole piece rests on a single source — one participant's first-person account written afterwards; the voyage section was written from scanty day-by-day notes (mostly distances, positions and weather) together with memory. Dialogue and psychology are reported rather than transcribed, need not be verbatim, and cannot be verified; the only day counts used are the sixth day out and the fourteenth day after leaving Elephant Island, as stated in the original, dates follow the original (May 8 and May 10), and the quoted passages give no calendar year, so none is supplied; distances, rations and water figures follow the original wording; the source is a scanned print in OCR, with individual words occasionally garbled, and quotations follow it as printed.
